skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: At T2 the interviewer, at the very start, said the firm represents the Committee and the company only, not the witness personally, and cannot give legal advice. The Upjohn warning was given before any substantive questions.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: At T2 the interviewer explained that the privilege belongs to the company, the company decides whether to waive it, and it may disclose what is learned without the witness's consent. The witness restated this at T5.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: At T6 the interviewer explained how the interview would proceed, asked for complete answers, set ground rules for speculation and estimates, and asked the witness to separate recollection from reconstruction.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: At T4 the interviewer asked the witness to state in his own words who the firm represents and who controls the privilege, and invited questions at T2. The witness's restatement at T5 confirmed his understanding.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: At T64 and T68 the interviewer asked whether there was anything else, reminded the witness to keep documents and notes, keep the interview confidential, not discuss it with other witnesses, and said they may follow up.

moments.text: To be clear, we represent the Committee and the company only. We do not represent you personally, we are not your attorney, and we can't give you legal advice.
that privilege belongs to the company, not to you or to us.
could you tell me in your own words your understanding of who we represent, and who controls the privilege?
Explained how the interview would proceed, asked for complete answers, set ground rules for speculation and estimates, and asked the witness to say whether he remembered or was reconstructing.
Is there anything I haven't asked about that you think the Committee should know?
Please keep all related documents and notes, keep today confidential, and don't discuss it with other witnesses.

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: At T14 the interviewer gave an open invitation to tell everything about how LJM1 came about, and at T16 and T18 let the witness keep going, but later sections were mostly narrow questions.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: The interview moved from role (T8) to reporting lines (T12), then to LJM1 (T14), the Board presentation (T22), Southampton (T30) and Chewco (T46), which is a sensible general-to-specific order.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Most questions were clear, such as who raised the idea at T20. Some were compound, such as T34 asking what the Foundation put in and what it received, and T46 asking about Kopper's selection.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: The interviewer stayed neutral and polite throughout, for example at T38 and T40, and kept control of the interview when the witness wandered.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: The interviewer adjusted at T38 and T40 after the witness's answers on Southampton, but did not change technique when the witness repeated non-answers at T21, T29, and T49 to T51.

moments.text: Tell me everything you remember about how LJM1 came about in 1999.
Who first suggested that you serve as the general partner?
Who raised it with them first?
What did the Foundation put in, and what did it receive?
How does that fit with what you told the Board about not receiving value from the Enron stock?
How do you know Mr. Causey and Mr. Buy reviewed every LJM2 deal?

areas.name: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: The interviewer followed up the Southampton Board-representation conflict at T40 to T44, but let evasive answers stand at T21, T29 and T51, which repeated 'as I said' without pressing.

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: The interviewer established who invested in Southampton (T32 to T33), how much and when (T34 to T38), and who was told about it (T42 to T45).

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: The interviewer refreshed memory with the $4.5 million figure at T38 but did not try other ways when the witness said 'Raptor I is the one I remember' at T63, and did not use the Board resolution the witness cited.

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: At T56 to T59 the interviewer asked how the witness knew approvals were reviewed and whether he checked, and got a clear answer that he assumed it and did not check. This separated personal knowledge from assumption.

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: At T66 the interviewer asked who else should be spoken with and got a list of named witnesses at T67, including Causey, Buy, Glisan, Kopper and McMahon.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: The witness pointed to the Foundation's statements (T37), the Board resolution and minutes (T25), and approval sheets (T61 to T63), but the interviewer did not ask for or identify these records during the interview, only a general request at T68.

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: At T24 the interviewer asked how sure the witness was about what he told the Board, and at T38 checked the figure against the information they had.

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: The interviewer followed up material answers on Southampton at T40 to T45 and on the disclosure reason at T50, and asked 'Which ones?' at T62, but did not pursue several material responses further.

moments.text: How sure are you that's what you told them?
Asked who negotiated for LJM1; the witness answered only 'As I said, Michael and me' and the answer was not pressed.
Our information is roughly $4.5 million, about six weeks after it invested. Does that fit your memory?
Did you tell the Board, Mr. Lay, or Mr. Skilling about the Foundation's investment?
What were those disclosure considerations?
Did you check that it was followed?
Which ones?
Who else should we speak with?

skills.name: Effective Selection
skills.description: Selects and contextualizes documents effectively, and properly authenticates the document.
skills.reason: The only document shown was the Executive Committee minutes at T52, which the witness authenticated at T53. The interviewer did not show the Board resolution or minutes on the June 1999 representation even though the witness cited them at T25.

skills.name: Narrative
skills.description: Gets the witness's story first, before using conflicting evidence.
skills.reason: The interviewer first asked about the Chewco choice and disclosure (T46 to T51) before showing the minutes at T52, so the witness's account came first.

skills.name: Accuracy
skills.description: Describes the document accurately.
skills.reason: The description at T52 and the question at T54 were accurate and neutral, and the interviewer did not misstate what the minutes say.

skills.name: Avoid Initial Conclusion
skills.description: Separates the document from inferences or conclusions, unless the witness takes an unreasonable stance.
skills.reason: The question at T54 was neutral. The question at T56 presumed that approvals were not reviewed, which edged toward a conclusion.

skills.name: Fairness
skills.description: Provides the witness with a fair opportunity to explain any inconsistencies or disagreements with the document.
skills.reason: At T40 the interviewer asked how the Foundation's investment fits with what the witness told the Board, which gave the witness a fair chance to explain, and he did so at T41.

moments.text: I'd like to show you the minutes of the November 5, 1997 Executive Committee meeting. Do you recognize them?
The witness recognized the minutes as the Committee's minutes from that call, prepared by the Corporate Secretary's office, which authenticated them.
Do they mention Mr. Kopper's role in Chewco?

missed_opportunities: T25: The witness said the Board representation is in the resolution and minutes, which bear directly on what the Board was told about his compensation. The interviewer accepted 'Very sure' and never showed or asked for those documents, so the key conflict was left untested.

T49: After the witness said avoiding proxy disclosure was one of the main reasons, and then repeated only 'The proxy disclosure, as I said' at T51, the interviewer did not change approach. They did not press who chose Kopper, what Fastow's own financial connection to Chewco was, or whether the Board was told.
tips: After he says the Board resolution and minutes support his account, ask: What words in those documents do you rely on, and would you read the relevant passage with me now so we can compare it to what you told us?

When a witness repeats an answer, ask: What other reasons were there besides avoiding proxy disclosure, who made the decision to use Michael Kopper, and what financial interest, if any, did you have in Chewco?
